title: He Jumped From 25,000 Feet With No Parachute
description: AI-narrated commentary breaking down the physics and prep behind one of the wildest stunts ever attempted: a freefall from 25,000 feet with no parachute, no wingsuit -- just a net and two years of practice.

beats.text: One man jumped out of a plane at 25,000 feet with zero parachute, zero wingsuit -- just his body and a net.
That's a two-minute freefall, hitting speeds over 120 miles per hour before impact.
The net was about the size of a football field -- miss it by a few feet and there's no second attempt.
He trained for over two years, using GPS markers and practice jumps to nail the exact angle and timing.
The real skill wasn't the fall -- it was staying perfectly still and flat, because any wobble changes your landing spot.
It's a reminder that the scariest stunts are usually the most rehearsed, not the most reckless.
Would you trust two years of practice enough to skip the parachute? Drop your honest answer below.
